prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Finding a crypto education site that uses plain English, shows real money, and **actively publishes its losses** is rare because most crypto sites are trying to sell you a course, a token, or referral links. 

However, there is one project that stands out above all others for meeting **every single one** of your criteria, alongside a runner-up newsletter.

---

### 1. The Absolute Best Match: **Top 10 Crypto Index Fund Experiments**
* **Website:** [top10cryptos.com](https://top10cryptos.com/) (also published on Reddit as *u/Joe-M-4*)

This is widely considered the most honest, transparent, and educational project in the crypto space for beginners. 

* **The Concept:** Starting in January 2018, the creator (Joe) bought $100 of each of the Top 10 cryptocurrencies ($1,000 total). He has repeated this experiment every single January 1st (2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025). He does not trade; he simply holds.
* **Why it fits your criteria:**
  * **Plain English:** Written in a conversational, humorous, self-deprecating style that anyone can understand. No confusing jargon or technical chart analysis.
  * **Real Numbers:** Tracks the exact dollar amounts, percentage gains, and overall portfolio values month-by-month for over 7 years.
  * **Publishes Losses (Brutally Honest):** This is where it shines. He openly tracks projects that lost 90%+ of their value, coins that went completely to zero (like Terra LUNA and FTX's FTT), and long periods where his entire portfolio was deep in the red. He explicitly shows how hard it is to beat plain Bitcoin.

---

### 2. Best for Daily Plain-English News & Lessons: **Milk Road**
* **Website:** [milkroad.com](https://www.milkroad.com/)

If you are looking for a regular newsletter/website to learn how the crypto ecosystem works day-to-day, *Milk Road* is built specifically for beginners.

* **Why it fits your criteria:**
  * **Plain English:** They use memes, simple analogies, and a 5th-grade reading level to explain complex concepts (like DeFi, staking, or ETF approvals). 
  * **Real Numbers & Losses:** The founders originally launched the "Milk Road Portfolio," where they publicly tracked their own trades using real money. They openly discussed when they lost money, bought at the top, or got burned by bad market conditions. While the site has grown into a broader media company, its core ethos remains focused on warning beginners about risks and showing real market downside rather than hype.

---

### 3. Best for Pure Concepts (No Hype): **99Bitcoins**
* **Website:** [99bitcoins.com](https://99bitcoins.com/)

If you just need to understand *what* a blockchain is, *what* gas fees are, or *how* a wallet works:

* **Why it fits:** It is famous for its "Bitcoin for Beginners" non-technical approach. 
* **The Catch:** While it explains concepts in ultra-plain English and has an infamous **"Bitcoin Obituary"** page (tracking every time mainstream media declared crypto "dead"), it does *not* run a live portfolio where it tracks its own real-money losses.

---

### Summary Recommendation

If you want **real numbers, plain English, and total transparency on losses**, start reading **[Top 10 Crypto Index Fund Experiments](https://top10cryptos.com/)**. Reading through his monthly updates from 2018 to the present will give you a better, more realistic education on crypto cycles than almost any paid course on the internet.
